newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania says three towns "out of control" - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Albania says three towns "out of control" - Dini.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Wednesday he had been told by his Albanian counterpart Tritan Shehu that the situation in the southern towns of Vlore, Sarande and Delvine was "out of control".

Dini was speaking to the foreign affairs committee of the Senate (upper house of parliament) after a telephone call with Shehu in which the Albanian minister said insurgents had seized three armoured vehicles.

Dini quoted Shehu as saying that "the police and the armed forces have orders to isolate the places where rebels are concentrated, avoiding engaging in armed conflict". Shehu said that there had been no new victims, Dini added.
Albania has imposed a state of emergency to quash an armed rebellion in the south sparked by the collapse of dubious savings schemes. Some 20 people are reported to have died.
Dini told Reuters Television later that the European Union might consider sending troops to Albania but would only do so if requested by Tirana.
"There is no such request," Dini said. "There is no alternative to a political solution."

Fighting was reported near the Adriatic town of Sarande on Wednesday. Army forces secured roads to the flashpoint coastal town of Vlore and the mountainous route between Gjirokaster and Sarande, a government information official said in Tirana.

Eyewitnesses reported clashes between insurgents and army units between Sarande and Delvine, 20 km (12 miles) to the east, throughout the morning. An eyewitness said rebels had seized an army tank in Sarande and were driving it through the streets.
Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo, whose country holds the current presidency of the EU, is going to Albania on Friday for emergency talks on the crisis in Europe's poorest state.
Dini said the entire EU was committed to finding a way to end the strife through dialogue.
"Dialogue is difficult, there is distrust and no mutual recognition between the government and the opposition that has made dialogue between the parties difficult so far but not impossible," he said.

Dini was quoted in an interview with Wednesday's La Repubblica newspaper as saying European governments have asked Albanian President Sali Berisha to form a cross-party administration and hold a fresh general election within 45 days.

"(The Italian government) is ready to send financial and technical aid to help an economic recovery and even soldiers -- a contingent to reinforce the Albanian forces and prevent organised crime taking advantage of the chaos and increasing the flow of illegal immigrants to Italy," Dini said.
"But to do all this we must have an Albanian government we can talk to," he added.
The government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi and his ministers resigned on Saturday.
